nodes.name: OffscreenCanvas.height
nodes.doc: The height of the canvas.

nodes.name: OffscreenCanvas.width
nodes.doc: The width of the canvas.

nodes.name: Performance
nodes.doc:
Deno supports User Timing Level 3
which is not widely supported yet in other runtimes.

Check out the
Performance API
documentation on MDN for further information about how to use the API.

nodes.name: Performance.mark
nodes.doc: Stores a timestamp with the associated name (a "mark").

nodes.name: Performance.measure
nodes.doc:
Stores the DOMHighResTimeStamp duration between two marks along with the
associated name (a "measure").

nodes.name: Performance.clearMarks
nodes.doc: Removes the stored timestamp with the associated name.

nodes.name: Performance.clearMeasures
nodes.doc: Removes stored timestamp with the associated name.

nodes.name: Performance.clearResourceTimings
nodes.doc:
Removes all performance entries with an entryType of "resource" from the
performance timeline and sets the size of the performance resource data
buffer to zero.

Note: Deno does not currently track resource timings, so this method has
no observable effect. It is provided for API compatibility.

nodes.name: Performance.setResourceTimingBufferSize
nodes.doc:
Sets the desired size of the browser's resource timing buffer which
stores the "resource" performance entries.

Note: Deno does not currently track resource timings, so this method has
no observable effect. It is provided for API compatibility.

nodes.name: Performance.mark
nodes.doc: Stores a timestamp with the associated name (a "mark").

nodes.name: Performance.measure
nodes.doc:
Stores the DOMHighResTimeStamp duration between two marks along with the
associated name (a "measure").

nodes.name: Performance.measure
nodes.doc:
Stores the DOMHighResTimeStamp duration between two marks along with the
associated name (a "measure").

nodes.name: Performance.now
Performance.toJSON
nodes.doc: Returns a JSON representation of the performance object.

nodes.name: Performance.timeOrigin
nodes.doc: Returns a timestamp representing the start of the performance measurement.

nodes.name: PerformanceEntry
nodes.doc:
Encapsulates a single performance metric that is part of the performance
timeline. A performance entry can be directly created by making a performance
mark or measure (for example by calling the .mark() method) at an explicit
point in an application.

nodes.name: PerformanceMark
nodes.doc:
PerformanceMark is an abstract interface for PerformanceEntry objects
with an entryType of "mark". Entries of this type are created by calling
performance.mark() to add a named DOMHighResTimeStamp (the mark) to the
performance timeline.

nodes.name: PerformanceMarkOptions
nodes.doc:
Options which are used in conjunction with performance.mark. Check out the
MDN
performance.mark()
documentation for more details.

nodes.name: PerformanceMarkOptions.detail
nodes.doc: Metadata to be included in the mark.

nodes.name: PerformanceMarkOptions.startTime
nodes.doc: Timestamp to be used as the mark time.

nodes.name: PerformanceMarkOptions.detail
nodes.doc: Metadata to be included in the mark.

nodes.name: PerformanceMarkOptions.startTime
nodes.doc: Timestamp to be used as the mark time.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasure
nodes.doc:
PerformanceMeasure is an abstract interface for PerformanceEntry objects
with an entryType of "measure". Entries of this type are created by calling
performance.measure() to add a named DOMHighResTimeStamp (the measure)
between two marks to the performance timeline.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions
nodes.doc:
Options which are used in conjunction with performance.measure. Check out the
MDN
performance.mark()
documentation for more details.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions.detail
nodes.doc: Metadata to be included in the measure.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions.start
nodes.doc:
Timestamp to be used as the start time or string to be used as start
mark.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions.duration
nodes.doc: Duration between the start and end times.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions.end
nodes.doc: Timestamp to be used as the end time or string to be used as end mark.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions.detail
nodes.doc: Metadata to be included in the measure.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions.start
nodes.doc:
Timestamp to be used as the start time or string to be used as start
mark.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions.duration
nodes.doc: Duration between the start and end times.

nodes.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions.end
nodes.doc: Timestamp to be used as the end time or string to be used as end mark.

nodes.name: PerformanceObserver
nodes.doc:
Observes performance measurement events and is notified of new
PerformanceEntry objects as they are recorded in the performance
timeline.

nodes.name: PerformanceObserver.disconnect
nodes.doc: Stops the observer from receiving any further performance entries.

nodes.name: PerformanceObserver.observe
nodes.doc: Specifies the set of performance entry types to observe.

nodes.name: PerformanceObserver.takeRecords
nodes.doc: Returns the current list of buffered performance entries, emptying it.

nodes.name: PerformanceObserverCallback
nodes.doc: The callback invoked when the observed set of performance entries grows.

nodes.name: PerformanceObserverEntryList
nodes.doc:
A list of PerformanceEntry objects passed to a
PerformanceObserver callback via its observe() method.

nodes.name: PerformanceObserverEntryList.getEntries
nodes.doc: Returns all explicitly observed performance entries.

nodes.name: PerformanceObserverEntryList.getEntriesByName
nodes.doc: Returns the observed performance entries with the given name.

nodes.name: PerformanceObserverEntryList.getEntriesByType
nodes.doc: Returns the observed performance entries with the given entry type.

nodes.name: PremultiplyAlpha
nodes.doc:
Specifies whether the bitmap's color channels should be premultiplied by
the alpha channel.

nodes.name: ProgressEvent
nodes.doc:
Events measuring progress of an underlying process, like an HTTP request
(for an XMLHttpRequest, or the loading of the underlying resource of an
, , ,  or ).

nodes.name: QuotaExceededError
nodes.doc: Represents an error when a quota has been exceeded.

nodes.name: ReadableStream
nodes.doc:
This Streams API interface represents a readable stream of byte data. The
Fetch API offers a concrete instance of a ReadableStream through the body
property of a Response object.

nodes.name: RegExpConstructor.escape
nodes.doc:
Returns a new string in which characters that are potentially special in a
regular expression pattern are replaced with escape sequences.

nodes.name: Request
nodes.doc: This Fetch API interface represents a resource request.

nodes.name: Request.cache
nodes.doc:
Returns the cache mode associated with request, which is a string
indicating how the request will interact with the browser's cache when
fetching.

nodes.name: Request.credentials
nodes.doc:
Returns the credentials mode associated with request, which is a string
indicating whether credentials will be sent with the request always, never,
or only when sent to a same-origin URL.

nodes.name: Request.destination
nodes.doc: Returns the kind of resource requested by request, e.g., "document" or "script".

nodes.name: Request.headers
nodes.doc:
Returns a Headers object consisting of the headers associated with request.
Note that headers added in the network layer by the user agent will not be
accounted for in this object, e.g., the "Host" header.

nodes.name: Request.integrity
nodes.doc:
Returns request's subresource integrity metadata, which is a cryptographic
hash of the resource being fetched. Its value consists of multiple hashes
separated by whitespace. [SRI]

nodes.name: Request.isHistoryNavigation
nodes.doc:
Returns a boolean indicating whether or not request is for a history
navigation (a.k.a. back-forward navigation).

nodes.name: Request.isReloadNavigation
nodes.doc:
Returns a boolean indicating whether or not request is for a reload
navigation, e.g. a refresh triggered via the browser's reload control or
by calling location.reload().

nodes.name: Request.keepalive
nodes.doc:
Returns a boolean indicating whether or not request can outlive the global
in which it was created.

nodes.name: Request.method
nodes.doc: Returns request's HTTP method, which is "GET" by default.

nodes.name: Request.mode
nodes.doc:
Returns the mode associated with request, which is a string indicating
whether the request will use CORS, or will be restricted to same-origin
URLs.

nodes.name: Request.redirect
nodes.doc:
Returns the redirect mode associated with request, which is a string
indicating how redirects for the request will be handled during fetching. A
request will follow redirects by default.

nodes.name: Request.referrer
nodes.doc:
Returns the referrer of request. Its value can be a same-origin URL if
explicitly set in init, the empty string to indicate no referrer, and
"about:client" when defaulting to the global's default. This is used during
fetching to determine the value of the Referer header of the request
being made.

nodes.name: Request.referrerPolicy
nodes.doc:
Returns the referrer policy associated with request. This is used during
fetching to compute the value of the request's referrer.

nodes.name: Request.signal
nodes.doc:
Returns the signal associated with request, which is an AbortSignal object
indicating whether or not request has been aborted, and its abort event
handler.

nodes.name: Request.url
nodes.doc: Returns the URL of request as a string.

nodes.name: RequestInit.body
nodes.doc: A BodyInit object or null to set request's body.

nodes.name: RequestInit.cache
nodes.doc:
A string indicating how the request will interact with the browser's cache
to set request's cache.

nodes.name: RequestInit.credentials
nodes.doc:
A string indicating whether credentials will be sent with the request
always, never, or only when sent to a same-origin URL. Sets request's
credentials.

nodes.name: RequestInit.headers
nodes.doc:
A Headers object, an object literal, or an array of two-item arrays to set
request's headers.

nodes.name: RequestInit.integrity
nodes.doc:
A cryptographic hash of the resource to be fetched by request. Sets
request's integrity.

nodes.name: RequestInit.keepalive
nodes.doc: A boolean to set request's keepalive.

nodes.name: RequestInit.method
nodes.doc: A string to set request's method.

nodes.name: RequestInit.mode
nodes.doc:
A string to indicate whether the request will use CORS, or will be
restricted to same-origin URLs. Sets request's mode.

nodes.name: RequestInit.priority
nodes.doc:
A string indicating the relative priority of the request. Sets request's
priority.

nodes.name: RequestInit.redirect
nodes.doc:
A string indicating whether request follows redirects, results in an error
upon encountering a redirect, or returns the redirect (in an opaque
fashion). Sets request's redirect.

nodes.name: RequestInit.referrer
nodes.doc:
A string whose value is a same-origin URL, "about:client", or the empty
string, to set request's referrer.

nodes.name: RequestInit.referrerPolicy
nodes.doc: A referrer policy to set request's referrerPolicy.

nodes.name: RequestInit.signal
nodes.doc: An AbortSignal to set request's signal.

nodes.name: RequestInit.window
nodes.doc: Can only be null. Used to disassociate request from any Window.

nodes.name: ResizeQuality
nodes.doc:
Specifies the algorithm to be used for resizing the input to match the
output dimensions. One of pixelated, low (default), medium, or high.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.doc: This Fetch API interface represents the response to a request.

nodes.name: Storage
nodes.doc:
This Web Storage API interface provides access to a particular domain's
session or local storage. It allows, for example, the addition, modification,
or deletion of stored data items.

nodes.name: Storage.clear
nodes.doc: Empties the list associated with the object of all key/value pairs, if there are any.

nodes.name: Storage.getItem
nodes.doc: Returns the current value associated with the given key, or null if the given key does not exist in the list associated with the object.

nodes.name: Storage.key
nodes.doc: Returns the name of the nth key in the list, or null if n is greater than or equal to the number of key/value pairs in the object.

nodes.name: Storage.removeItem
nodes.doc: Removes the key/value pair with the given key from the list associated with the object, if a key/value pair with the given key exists.

nodes.name: Storage.setItem
nodes.doc:
Sets the value of the pair identified by key to value, creating a new key/value pair if none existed for key previously.

Throws a "QuotaExceededError" DOMException exception if the new value couldn't be set. (Setting could fail if, e.g., the user has disabled storage for the site, or if the quota has been exceeded.)

nodes.name: Storage.length
nodes.doc: Returns the number of key/value pairs currently present in the list associated with the object.

nodes.name: StructuredSerializeOptions
nodes.doc:
Options that control structured serialization operations such as
structuredClone(value, options) and MessagePort.postMessage(message, options).

The optional transfer array lists Transferable objects whose
underlying resources should be moved (transferred) to the receiving side
instead of being cloned. After a successful transfer:

For an ArrayBuffer, the original buffer becomes neutered (its
byteLength is set to 0).

For a MessagePort, the port becomes unusable on the sending side and
future events will arrive only on the transferred port at the receiver.

Validation rules:

Each transferable may appear only once in the transfer list.

A MessagePort cannot be listed together with its counterpart port from
the same MessageChannel in the same transfer operation.

Duplicate or otherwise invalid entries will cause a DataCloneError
DOMException to be thrown.

Transferring improves performance for large binary data and allows moving
communication endpoints without copying.

nodes.name: StructuredSerializeOptions.transfer
nodes.doc: List of transferable objects whose ownership is moved instead of cloned.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto
nodes.doc:
This Web Crypto API interface provides a number of low-level cryptographic
functions. It is accessed via the Crypto.subtle properties available in a
window context (via globalThis.crypto).

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.generateKey
nodes.doc:
Generates an asymmetric cryptographic key pair for encryption, signing, or
key exchange.

This overload is used for generating key pairs with RSA or elliptic curve
algorithms.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.generateKey
nodes.doc:
Generates a symmetric cryptographic key for encryption, authentication, or
hashing.

This overload is used for algorithms such as AES and HMAC.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.generateKey
nodes.doc:
Generates a cryptographic key or key pair for a given algorithm.

This generic overload handles any key generation request, returning either
a symmetric key or an asymmetric key pair based on the provided algorithm.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.importKey
nodes.doc:
Imports a cryptographic key in JSON Web Key (JWK) format.

This method is used to import an asymmetric key (e.g., RSA or ECDSA) from a JWK object.
JWK allows structured representation of keys, making them portable across different systems.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.importKey
nodes.doc:
Imports a cryptographic key in raw, PKCS8, or SPKI format.

This method is used to import symmetric keys (e.g., AES), private keys (PKCS8), or public keys (SPKI).

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.exportKey
nodes.doc:
Exports a cryptographic key in JSON Web Key (JWK) format.

This method allows exporting an asymmetric key (e.g., RSA, ECDSA) into a JSON-based representation,
making it easy to store and transfer across systems.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.exportKey
nodes.doc:
Exports a cryptographic key in raw, PKCS8, or SPKI format.

This method is used to export symmetric keys (AES), private keys (PKCS8), or public keys (SPKI) in binary form.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.sign
nodes.doc:
Generates a digital signature using a private cryptographic key.

This method is used to sign data with an asymmetric key (e.g., RSA-PSS, ECDSA).

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.verify
nodes.doc:
Verifies a digital signature using a public cryptographic key.

This method checks whether a signature is valid for the given data.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.digest
nodes.doc:
Computes a cryptographic hash (digest) of the given data.

This method is commonly used for verifying data integrity.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.encrypt
nodes.doc:
Encrypts data using a cryptographic key.

This method is used with both symmetric (AES) and asymmetric (RSA) encryption.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.decrypt
nodes.doc: Decrypts previously encrypted data using a cryptographic key.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.deriveBits
nodes.doc: This method is used to derive a key from a base key using a cryptographic algorithm.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.deriveKey
nodes.doc:
This method is used to derive a secret key from a base or master key using a cryptographic algorithm.
It returns a Promise which fulfils with an object of the new key.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.wrapKey
nodes.doc: Wraps (encrypts) a cryptographic key for secure storage or transmission

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.unwrapKey
nodes.doc: Unwraps (decrypts) a previously wrapped key.

nodes.name: SubtleCrypto.supports
nodes.doc:
Synchronous feature detection for Web Crypto algorithm/operation
combinations, per the WICG "Modern Algorithms in the Web Crypto API"
proposal. Returns true when this runtime implements the requested
combination, false otherwise.

The third argument is interpreted as the derived-bit length when it is
a number (relevant for "deriveBits"), and as a related algorithm —
e.g. the derived-key algorithm for "deriveKey", the wrapped/unwrapped
key algorithm for "wrapKey" / "unwrapKey", or the shared-key
algorithm for "encapsulateKey" / "decapsulateKey" — otherwise.

nodes.name: TextDecoder
nodes.doc:
Represents a decoder for a specific text encoding, allowing you to convert
binary data into a string given the encoding.

nodes.name: TextDecoder.decode
nodes.doc:
Turns binary data, often in the form of a Uint8Array, into a string given
the encoding.

nodes.name: TextDecoderCommon.encoding
nodes.doc: Returns encoding's name, lowercased.

nodes.name: TextDecoderCommon.fatal
nodes.doc: Returns true if error mode is "fatal", otherwise false.

nodes.name: TextDecoderCommon.ignoreBOM
nodes.doc: Returns the value of ignore BOM.

nodes.name: TextEncoder
nodes.doc:
Allows you to convert a string into binary data (in the form of a Uint8Array)
given the encoding.

nodes.name: TextEncoder.encode
nodes.doc: Turns a string into binary data (in the form of a Uint8Array) using UTF-8 encoding.

nodes.name: TextEncoder.encodeInto
nodes.doc: Encodes a string into the destination Uint8Array and returns the result of the encoding.

nodes.name: TextEncoderCommon.encoding
nodes.doc: Returns "utf-8".

nodes.name: UADataValues
nodes.doc: The values returned by NavigatorUAData.getHighEntropyValues.

nodes.name: UALowEntropyJSON
nodes.doc: The low-entropy values returned by NavigatorUAData.toJSON.

nodes.name: URL
nodes.doc:
The URL interface represents an object providing static methods used for
creating, parsing, and manipulating URLs in Deno.

Use the URL API for safely parsing, constructing, normalizing, and encoding URLs.
This is the preferred way to work with URLs in Deno rather than manual string
manipulation which can lead to errors and security issues.

nodes.name: URL.toString
nodes.doc: The toString() method of the URL interface returns a string containing the complete URL.

nodes.name: URL.toJSON
nodes.doc: The toJSON() method of the URL interface returns a JSON representation of the URL.

nodes.name: URL.hash
nodes.doc:
The hash property of the URL interface is a string that starts with a # and is followed by the fragment identifier of the URL.
It returns an empty string if the URL does not contain a fragment identifier.

nodes.name: URL.host
nodes.doc: The host property of the URL interface is a string that includes the URL.hostname and the URL.port if one is specified in the URL includes by including a : followed by the port number.

nodes.name: URL.hostname
nodes.doc: The hostname property of the URL interface is a string that represents the fully qualified domain name of the URL.

nodes.name: URL.href
nodes.doc: The href property of the URL interface is a string that represents the complete URL.

nodes.name: URL.origin
nodes.doc: The origin property of the URL interface is a string that represents the origin of the URL, that is the URL.protocol, URL.host, and URL.port.

nodes.name: URL.password
nodes.doc: The password property of the URL interface is a string that represents the password specified in the URL.

nodes.name: URL.pathname
nodes.doc: The pathname property of the URL interface is a string that represents the path of the URL.

nodes.name: URL.port
nodes.doc: The port property of the URL interface is a string that represents the port of the URL if an explicit port has been specified in the URL.

nodes.name: URL.protocol
nodes.doc: The protocol property of the URL interface is a string that represents the protocol scheme of the URL and includes a trailing :.

nodes.name: URL.search
nodes.doc:
The search property of the URL interface is a string that represents the search string, or the query string, of the URL.
This includes the ? character and the but excludes identifiers within the represented resource such as the URL.hash. More granular control can be found using URL.searchParams property.

nodes.name: URL.searchParams
nodes.doc:
The searchParams property of the URL interface provides a direct interface to
query parameters through a URLSearchParams object.

This property offers a convenient way to:

Parse URL query parameters

Manipulate query strings

Add, modify, or delete URL parameters

Work with form data in a URL-encoded format

Handle query string encoding/decoding automatically

nodes.name: URL.username
nodes.doc: The username property of the URL interface is a string that represents the username of the URL.

nodes.name: URL.parse
nodes.doc: Parses a URL string or URL object and returns a URL object.

nodes.name: URL.canParse
nodes.doc: Returns a boolean value indicating if a URL string is valid and can be parsed.

nodes.name: URL.createObjectURL
nodes.doc:
Creates a unique, temporary URL that represents a given Blob, File, or MediaSource object.

This method is particularly useful for:

Creating URLs for dynamically generated content

Working with blobs in a browser context

Creating workers from dynamically generated code

Setting up temporary URL references for file downloads

Note: Always call URL.revokeObjectURL() when you're done using the URL to prevent memory leaks.

nodes.name: URL.revokeObjectURL
nodes.doc:
Revokes a previously created object URL, freeing the memory associated with it.

Important for memory management in applications that create dynamic URLs.
Once an object URL is revoked:

It can no longer be used to fetch the content it referenced

The browser/runtime is allowed to release the memory or resources associated with it

Workers created via the URL will continue to run, but the URL becomes invalid for new creations

For security and performance in Deno applications, always revoke object URLs as soon as
they're no longer needed, especially when processing large files or generating many URLs.

nodes.name: URLPattern
nodes.doc:
The URLPattern API provides a web platform primitive for matching URLs based
on a convenient pattern syntax.

Common use cases for URLPattern include:

Building routers for web applications

Pattern-matching URLs for middleware

Extracting parameters from URL paths

URL-based feature toggles

Routing in serverless and edge functions

The syntax is based on path-to-regexp, supporting wildcards, named capture groups,
regular groups, and group modifiers - similar to Express.js route patterns.

nodes.name: URLPattern.test
URLPattern.exec
URLPattern.protocol
nodes.doc: The pattern string for the protocol.

nodes.name: URLPattern.username
nodes.doc: The pattern string for the username.

nodes.name: URLPattern.password
nodes.doc: The pattern string for the password.

nodes.name: URLPattern.hostname
nodes.doc: The pattern string for the hostname.

nodes.name: URLPattern.port
nodes.doc: The pattern string for the port.

nodes.name: URLPattern.pathname
nodes.doc: The pattern string for the pathname.

nodes.name: URLPattern.search
nodes.doc: The pattern string for the search.

nodes.name: URLPattern.hash
nodes.doc: The pattern string for the hash.

nodes.name: URLPattern.hasRegExpGroups
nodes.doc: Whether or not any of the specified groups use regexp groups.

nodes.name: URLPatternOptions
nodes.doc: Options for the URLPattern constructor.

nodes.name: URLPatternOptions.ignoreCase
nodes.doc: Enables case-insensitive matching.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult
nodes.doc: URLPatternResult is the object returned from URLPattern.exec.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult.inputs
nodes.doc: The inputs provided when matching.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult.protocol
nodes.doc: The matched result for the protocol matcher.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult.username
nodes.doc: The matched result for the username matcher.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult.password
nodes.doc: The matched result for the password matcher.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult.hostname
nodes.doc: The matched result for the hostname matcher.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult.port
nodes.doc: The matched result for the port matcher.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult.pathname
nodes.doc: The matched result for the pathname matcher.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult.search
nodes.doc: The matched result for the search matcher.

nodes.name: URLPatternResult.hash
nodes.doc: The matched result for the hash matcher.

nodes.name: URLSearchParams
nodes.doc:
URLSearchParams provides methods for working with the query string of a URL.

Use this interface to:

Parse query parameters from URLs

Build and modify query strings

Handle form data (when used with FormData)

Safely encode/decode URL parameter values

nodes.name: URLSearchParams.append
URLSearchParams.delete
URLSearchParams.getAll
URLSearchParams.get
nodes.doc:
Returns the first value associated to the given search parameter.

searchParams.get('name');

nodes.name: URLSearchParams.has
URLSearchParams.set
nodes.doc:
Sets the value associated with a given search parameter to the
given value. If there were several matching values, this method
deletes the others. If the search parameter doesn't exist, this
method creates it.

searchParams.set('name', 'value');

nodes.name: URLSearchParams.sort
nodes.doc:
Sort all key/value pairs contained in this object in place and
return undefined. The sort order is according to Unicode code
points of the keys.

searchParams.sort();

nodes.name: URLSearchParams.forEach
URLSearchParams.keys
URLSearchParams.values
URLSearchParams.entries
URLSearchParams.[Symbol.iterator]
URLSearchParams.toString
nodes.doc:
Returns a query string suitable for use in a URL.

searchParams.toString();

nodes.name: URLSearchParams.size
nodes.doc:
Contains the number of search parameters

searchParams.size

nodes.name: URLSearchParamsIterator
nodes.doc: Iterator for the URLSearchParams class, used to iterate over key-value pairs in search parameters.

nodes.name: Uint8Array.toBase64
nodes.doc:
Converts this Uint8Array object to a base64 string.

MDN

nodes.name: Uint8Array.setFromBase64
nodes.doc:
Populates this Uint8Array object with data from a base64 string.

MDN

nodes.name: Uint8Array.toHex
nodes.doc:
Converts this Uint8Array object to a hex string.

MDN

nodes.name: Uint8Array.setFromHex
nodes.doc:
Populates this Uint8Array object with data from a hex string.

MDN

nodes.name: Uint8ArrayConstructor.fromBase64
nodes.doc:
Creates a new Uint8Array object from a base64 string.

MDN

nodes.name: Uint8ArrayConstructor.fromHex
nodes.doc:
Creates a new Uint8Array object from a hex string.

MDN

nodes.name: WebAssembly
nodes.doc:
The WebAssembly JavaScript object acts as the namespace for all
WebAssembly-related
functionality. Unlike most global objects, it is not a constructor; it groups
the functions used to compile and instantiate WebAssembly modules together
with the classes (Module, Instance, Memory, Table, Global) and
error types used to work with them.

MDN

nodes.name: WebAssembly.CompileError
nodes.doc:
The WebAssembly.CompileError object indicates an error during WebAssembly decoding or validation.

MDN

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ExportValue
nodes.doc: A value that can be exported from a WebAssembly module instance.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Exports
nodes.doc:
The set of values exported by a WebAssembly module instance, keyed by
export name.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Global
nodes.doc:
A WebAssembly.Global object represents a global variable instance, accessible from
both JavaScript and importable/exportable across one or more WebAssembly.Module
instances. This allows dynamic linking of multiple modules.

MDN

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Global.prototype.valueOf
nodes.doc: Old-style method that returns the value contained inside the global variable.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Global.prototype.value
nodes.doc:
The value contained inside the global variable — this can be used to directly set
and get the global's value.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.GlobalDescriptor
nodes.doc:
The GlobalDescriptor describes the options you can pass to
new WebAssembly.Global().

nodes.name: WebAssembly.GlobalDescriptor.mutable
nodes.doc:
Whether the global variable can be modified after creation. Defaults to
false.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.GlobalDescriptor.value
nodes.doc: The data type of the global variable.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ImportExportKind
nodes.doc: The kind of entity referenced by a module import or export descriptor.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ImportValue
nodes.doc: A value that can be supplied to a WebAssembly module as an import.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Imports
nodes.doc:
The import object supplied when instantiating a WebAssembly module,
grouping imported values by module name.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Instance
nodes.doc:
A WebAssembly.Instance object is a stateful, executable instance of a WebAssembly.Module.
Instance objects contain all the Exported WebAssembly functions that allow calling into
WebAssembly code from JavaScript.

MDN

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Instance.prototype.exports
nodes.doc:
Returns an object containing as its members all the functions exported from the
WebAssembly module instance, to allow them to be accessed and used by JavaScript.
Read-only.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.LinkError
nodes.doc:
The WebAssembly.LinkError object indicates an error during module instantiation
(besides traps from the start function).

MDN

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Memory
nodes.doc:
The WebAssembly.Memory object is a resizable ArrayBuffer or SharedArrayBuffer that
holds the raw bytes of memory accessed by a WebAssembly Instance.

A memory created by JavaScript or in WebAssembly code will be accessible and mutable
from both JavaScript and WebAssembly.

MDN

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Memory.prototype.grow
nodes.doc:
Increases the size of the memory instance by a specified number of WebAssembly
pages (each one is 64KB in size).

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Memory.prototype.buffer
nodes.doc: An accessor property that returns the buffer contained in the memory.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.MemoryDescriptor
nodes.doc:
The MemoryDescriptor describes the options you can pass to
new WebAssembly.Memory().

nodes.name: WebAssembly.MemoryDescriptor.initial
nodes.doc:
The initial size of the memory, in units of WebAssembly pages (64KB
each).

nodes.name: WebAssembly.MemoryDescriptor.maximum
nodes.doc:
The maximum size the memory is allowed to grow to, in units of
WebAssembly pages.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.MemoryDescriptor.shared
nodes.doc:
Whether the memory is shared between agents (backed by a
SharedArrayBuffer). Defaults to false.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Module
nodes.doc:
A WebAssembly.Module object contains stateless WebAssembly code that has already been compiled
by the browser — this can be efficiently shared with Workers, and instantiated multiple times.

MDN

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Module.customSections
nodes.doc:
Given a Module and string, returns a copy of the contents of all custom sections in the
module with the given string name.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Module.exports
nodes.doc: Given a Module, returns an array containing descriptions of all the declared exports.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Module.imports
nodes.doc: Given a Module, returns an array containing descriptions of all the declared imports.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ModuleExportDescriptor
nodes.doc:
A ModuleExportDescriptor is the description of a declared export in a
WebAssembly.Module.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ModuleExportDescriptor.kind
nodes.doc: The kind of entity being exported.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ModuleExportDescriptor.name
nodes.doc: The name under which the entity is exported.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ModuleImportDescriptor
nodes.doc:
A ModuleImportDescriptor is the description of a declared import in a
WebAssembly.Module.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ModuleImportDescriptor.kind
nodes.doc: The kind of entity being imported.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ModuleImportDescriptor.module
nodes.doc: The name of the module the entity is imported from.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ModuleImportDescriptor.name
nodes.doc: The name of the imported entity within its module.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.ModuleImports
nodes.doc: The set of values imported from a single module, keyed by import name.

nodes.name: WebAssembly.RuntimeError
nodes.doc:
The WebAssembly.RuntimeError object is the error type that is thrown whenever WebAssembly
specifies a trap.

MDN

nodes.name: WebAssembly.Table
nodes.doc:
The WebAssembly.Table() object is a JavaScript wrapper object — an array-like structure

nodes.doc:
Returns the extensions selected by the server, if any.

WebSocket extensions add optional features negotiated during the handshake via
the Sec-WebSocket-Extensions header.

At the time of writing, there are two registered extensions:

permessage-deflate: Enables per-message compression using DEFLATE.

bbf-usp-protocol: Used by the Broadband Forum's User Services Platform (USP).

See the full list at IANA WebSocket Extensions.

Example:

const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8080");
console.log(ws.extensions); // e.g., "permessage-deflate"

nodes.name: Window
nodes.doc:
Represents the global window object in the Deno runtime environment.

While Deno doesn't have a browser window, this interface mimics browser window
functionality for compatibility with web APIs. It provides access to global
properties and methods such as timers, storage, and event handling.

nodes.name: WindowEventMap
nodes.doc:
Defines the mapping between event names and their corresponding event types
for the Window interface in Deno.

This interface provides type safety for event handlers by associating event names
with their proper event types.

nodes.name: Worker
nodes.doc:
The Worker interface represents a background task that can be created via the
new Worker() constructor. Workers run in a separate thread, allowing for parallel execution
without blocking the main thread.

Workers can be used to:

Perform CPU-intensive calculations

Process large datasets

Handle tasks in parallel with the main execution thread

Run code in isolation with its own event loop

localStorage
nodes.doc:
Deno's localStorage API provides a way to store key-value pairs in a
web-like environment, similar to the Web Storage API found in browsers.
It allows developers to persist data across sessions in a Deno application.
This API is particularly useful for applications that require a simple
and effective way to store data locally.

Key-Value Storage: Stores data as key-value pairs.

Persistent: Data is retained even after the application is closed.

Synchronous API: Operations are performed synchronously.

localStorage is similar to sessionStorage, and shares the same
API methods, visible in the Storage type.

When using the --location flag, the origin for the location is used to
uniquely store the data. That means a location of http://example.com/a.ts
and http://example.com/b.ts and http://example.com:80/ would all share the
same storage, but https://example.com/ would be different.

For more information, see the reference guide for
Web Storage
and using
the --location flag.

Accessing it without --location throws.

nodes.name: onload

Load event handler for the window.
In Deno, this is primarily for API compatibility with browsers.

nodes.name: onunload

In Deno, this is primarily for API compatibility with browsers.

nodes.name: prompt
nodes.doc:
Shows the given message and waits for the user's input. Returns the user's input as string.

If the default value is given and the user inputs the empty string, then it returns the given
default value.

If the default value is not given and the user inputs the empty string, it returns the empty
string.

If the stdin is not interactive, it returns null.

nodes.name: queueMicrotask
nodes.doc:
A microtask is a short function which is executed after the function or
module which created it exits and only if the JavaScript execution stack is
empty, but before returning control to the event loop being used to drive the
script's execution environment. This event loop may be either the main event
loop or the event loop driving a web worker.

queueMicrotask(() => { console.log('This event loop stack is complete'); });

Equivalent to the global window object in browser environments.

nodes.name: sessionStorage
nodes.doc:
Deno's sessionStorage API operates similarly to the localStorage API,
but it is intended for storing data temporarily for the duration of a session.
Data stored in sessionStorage is cleared when the application session or
process ends. This makes it suitable for temporary data that you do not need
to persist across user sessions.

Key-Value Storage: Stores data as key-value pairs.

Session-Based: Data is only available for the duration of the page session.

Synchronous API: Operations are performed synchronously.

sessionStorage is similar to localStorage, and shares the same API
methods, visible in the Storage type.

For more information, see the reference guide for
Web Storage

nodes.name: structuredClone
nodes.doc:
Creates a deep copy of a given value using the structured clone algorithm.

Unlike a shallow copy, a deep copy does not hold the same references as the
source object, meaning its properties can be changed without affecting the
source. For more details, see
MDN.

Throws a DataCloneError if any part of the input value is not
serializable.

value.docs:
The URLPattern API provides a web platform primitive for matching URLs based on a convenient pattern syntax.

Common use cases for URLPattern include:

  • Building routers for web applications
  • Pattern-matching URLs for middleware
  • Extracting parameters from URL paths
  • URL-based feature toggles
  • Routing in serverless and edge functions

The syntax is based on path-to-regexp, supporting wildcards, named capture groups, regular groups, and group modifiers - similar to Express.js route patterns.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Basic routing with URLPattern (similar to Express.js)
const routes = [
  new URLPattern({ pathname: "/users" }),
  new URLPattern({ pathname: "/users/:id" }),
  new URLPattern({ pathname: "/products/:category/:id?" }),
];

// Check incoming request against routes
function handleRequest(req: Request) {
  const url = new URL(req.url);

  for (const route of routes) {
    const match = route.exec(url);
    if (match) {
      // Extract parameters from the URL
      const params = match.pathname.groups;
      return new Response(`Matched: ${JSON.stringify(params)}`);
    }
  }

  return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });
}

content.title: Example 2
content.markdown_body:
// Matching different URL parts
const apiPattern = new URLPattern({
  protocol: "https",
  hostname: "api.example.com",
  pathname: "/v:version/:resource/:id?",
  search: "*", // Match any query string
});

const match = apiPattern.exec("https://api.example.com/v1/users/123?format=json");
if (match) {
  console.log(match.pathname.groups.version); // "1"
  console.log(match.pathname.groups.resource); // "users"
  console.log(match.pathname.groups.id); // "123"
}

content.name: test
content.js_doc:
Test if the given input matches the stored pattern.

The input can either be provided as an absolute URL string with an optional base, relative URL string with a required base, or as individual components in the form of an URLPatternInit object.

const pattern = new URLPattern("https://example.com/books/:id");

// Test an absolute url string.
console.log(pattern.test("https://example.com/books/123")); // true

// Test a relative url with a base.
console.log(pattern.test("/books/123", "https://example.com")); // true

// Test an object of url components.
console.log(pattern.test({ pathname: "/books/123" })); // true

content.name: exec
content.js_doc:
Match the given input against the stored pattern.

The input can either be provided as an absolute URL string with an optional base, relative URL string with a required base, or as individual components in the form of an URLPatternInit object.

const pattern = new URLPattern("https://example.com/books/:id");

// Match an absolute url string.
let match = pattern.exec("https://example.com/books/123");
console.log(match.pathname.groups.id); // 123

// Match a relative url with a base.
match = pattern.exec("/books/123", "https://example.com");
console.log(match.pathname.groups.id); // 123

// Match an object of url components.
match = pattern.exec({ pathname: "/books/123" });
console.log(match.pathname.groups.id); // 123

value.docs:
The URLPattern API provides a web platform primitive for matching URLs based on a convenient pattern syntax.

The syntax is based on path-to-regexp. Wildcards, named capture groups, regular groups, and group modifiers are all supported.

// Specify the pattern as structured data.
const pattern = new URLPattern({ pathname: "/users/:user" });
const match = pattern.exec("https://blog.example.com/users/joe");
console.log(match.pathname.groups.user); // joe

// Specify a fully qualified string pattern.
const pattern = new URLPattern("https://example.com/books/:id");
console.log(pattern.test("https://example.com/books/123")); // true
console.log(pattern.test("https://deno.land/books/123")); // false

// Specify a relative string pattern with a base URL.
const pattern = new URLPattern("/article/:id", "https://blog.example.com");
console.log(pattern.test("https://blog.example.com/article")); // false
console.log(pattern.test("https://blog.example.com/article/123")); // true

value.docs:
Options that control structured serialization operations such as structuredClone(value, options) and MessagePort.postMessage(message, options).

The optional transfer array lists Transferable objects whose underlying resources should be moved (transferred) to the receiving side instead of being cloned. After a successful transfer:

  • For an ArrayBuffer, the original buffer becomes neutered (its byteLength is set to 0).
  • For a MessagePort, the port becomes unusable on the sending side and future events will arrive only on the transferred port at the receiver.

Validation rules:

  • Each transferable may appear only once in the transfer list.
  • A MessagePort cannot be listed together with its counterpart port from the same MessageChannel in the same transfer operation.
  • Duplicate or otherwise invalid entries will cause a DataCloneError DOMException to be thrown.

Transferring improves performance for large binary data and allows moving communication endpoints without copying.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Transferring an ArrayBuffer (zero-copy for large data)
const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(16);
const cloned = structuredClone(buffer, { transfer: [buffer] });

// After transfer, the original buffer is neutered
console.log(buffer.byteLength); // 0
console.log(cloned.byteLength); // 16

content.name: transfer
content.js_doc: List of transferable objects whose ownership is moved instead of cloned.

value.docs: Represents a queue to submit commands to the GPU.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Get a queue from the device (each device has a default queue)
const queue = device.queue;

// Write data to a buffer
const buffer = device.createBuffer({
  size: data.byteLength,
  usage: GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST | GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE
});
queue.writeBuffer(buffer, 0, data);

// Submit command buffers to the GPU for execution
const commandBuffer = commandEncoder.finish();
queue.submit([commandBuffer]);

// Wait for all submitted operations to complete
await queue.onSubmittedWorkDone();

// Example: Write data to a texture
const texture = device.createTexture({
  size: { width: 256, height: 256 },
  format: "rgba8unorm",
  usage: GPUTextureUsage.TEXTURE_BINDING | GPUTextureUsage.COPY_DST
});

const data = new Uint8Array(256 * 256 * 4); // RGBA data
// Fill data with your texture content...

queue.writeTexture(
  { texture },
  data,
  { bytesPerRow: 256 * 4 },
  { width: 256, height: 256 }
);

URLSearchParams provides methods for working with the query string of a URL.

Use this interface to:

  • Parse query parameters from URLs
  • Build and modify query strings
  • Handle form data (when used with FormData)
  • Safely encode/decode URL parameter values

content.name: size
content.js_doc:
Contains the number of search parameters

searchParams.size

content.name: append
content.js_doc:
Appends a specified key/value pair as a new search parameter.

let searchParams = new URLSearchParams();
searchParams.append('name', 'first');
searchParams.append('name', 'second');

content.name: delete
content.js_doc:
Deletes search parameters that match a name, and optional value, from the list of all search parameters.

let searchParams = new URLSearchParams([['name', 'value']]);
searchParams.delete('name');
searchParams.delete('name', 'value');

content.name: getAll
content.js_doc:
Returns all the values associated with a given search parameter as an array.

searchParams.getAll('name');

content.name: get
content.js_doc:
Returns the first value associated to the given search parameter.

searchParams.get('name');

content.name: has
content.js_doc:
Returns a boolean value indicating if a given parameter, or parameter and value pair, exists.

searchParams.has('name');
searchParams.has('name', 'value');

content.name: set
content.js_doc:
Sets the value associated with a given search parameter to the given value. If there were several matching values, this method deletes the others. If the search parameter doesn't exist, this method creates it.

searchParams.set('name', 'value');

content.name: sort
content.js_doc:
Sort all key/value pairs contained in this object in place and return undefined. The sort order is according to Unicode code points of the keys.

searchParams.sort();

content.name: forEach
content.js_doc:
Calls a function for each element contained in this object in place and return undefined. Optionally accepts an object to use as this when executing callback as second argument.

const params = new URLSearchParams([["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]]);
params.forEach((value, key, parent) => {
  console.log(value, key, parent);
});

content.name: keys
content.js_doc:
Returns an iterator allowing to go through all keys contained in this object.

const params = new URLSearchParams([["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]]);
for (const key of params.keys()) {
  console.log(key);
}

content.name: values
content.js_doc:
Returns an iterator allowing to go through all values contained in this object.

const params = new URLSearchParams([["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]]);
for (const value of params.values()) {
  console.log(value);
}

content.name: entries
content.js_doc:
Returns an iterator allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object.

const params = new URLSearchParams([["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]]);
for (const [key, value] of params.entries()) {
  console.log(key, value);
}

content.name: [[Symbol.iterator]]

Returns an iterator allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object.

const params = new URLSearchParams([["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]]);
for (const [key, value] of params) {
  console.log(key, value);
}

content.name: toString
content.js_doc:
Returns a query string suitable for use in a URL.

searchParams.toString();

Represents a part of a formatted date range produced by Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatRange().

Each part has a type and value that describes its role within the formatted string. The source property indicates whether the part comes from the start date, end date, or is shared between them.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
const dtf = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en', {
  dateStyle: 'long',
  timeStyle: 'short'
});
const parts = dtf.formatRangeToParts(
  new Date(2023, 0, 1, 12, 0),
  new Date(2023, 0, 3, 15, 30)
);
console.log(parts);
// Parts might include elements like:
// { type: 'month', value: 'January', source: 'startRange' }
// { type: 'day', value: '1', source: 'startRange' }
// { type: 'literal', value: ' - ', source: 'shared' }
// { type: 'day', value: '3', source: 'endRange' }
// ...

content.name: type

content.name: value

content.name: source
content.js_doc:
Indicates which date in the range this part comes from.

  • 'startRange': The part is from the start date
  • 'endRange': The part is from the end date
  • 'shared': The part is shared between both dates (like separators)

    namedCurve: "P-384",
  },
  true,
  ["sign"],
);

content.docs: Create a new ImageBitmap object from a given source.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
try {
  // Fetch an image
  const response = await fetch("https://example.com/image.png");
  const blob = await response.blob();

  // Basic usage
  const basicBitmap = await createImageBitmap(blob);
  console.log("Basic bitmap size:", basicBitmap.width, basicBitmap.height);

  // With options
  const resizedBitmap = await createImageBitmap(blob, {
    resizeWidth: 100,
    resizeHeight: 100,
    resizeQuality: "high",
    imageOrientation: "flipY"
  });

  // Cleanup when done
  basicBitmap.close();
  resizedBitmap.close();
} catch (error) {
  console.error("Failed to create ImageBitmap:", error);
}

}

When set to true, options's capture prevents callback from being invoked when the event's eventPhase attribute value is BUBBLING_PHASE. When false (or not present), callback will not be invoked when event's eventPhase attribute value is CAPTURING_PHASE. Either way, callback will be invoked if event's eventPhase attribute value is AT_TARGET.

When set to true, options's passive indicates that the callback will not cancel the event by invoking preventDefault(). This is used to enable performance optimizations described in § 2.8 Observing event listeners.

When set to true, options's once indicates that the callback will only be invoked once after which the event listener will be removed.

The event listener is appended to target's event listener list and is not appended if it has the same type, callback, and capture.

value.docs: Used to record GPU commands for later execution by the GPU.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Create a command encoder
const commandEncoder = device.createCommandEncoder({
  label: "Main Command Encoder"
});

// Record a copy from one buffer to another
commandEncoder.copyBufferToBuffer(
  sourceBuffer, 0, // Source buffer and offset
  destinationBuffer, 0, // Destination buffer and offset
  sourceBuffer.size // Size to copy
);

// Begin a compute pass to execute a compute shader
const computePass = commandEncoder.beginComputePass();
computePass.setPipeline(computePipeline);
computePass.setBindGroup(0, bindGroup);
computePass.dispatchWorkgroups(32, 1, 1); // Run 32 workgroups
computePass.end();

// Begin a render pass to draw to a texture
const renderPass = commandEncoder.beginRenderPass({
  colorAttachments: [{
    view: textureView,
    clearValue: { r: 0.0, g: 0.0, b: 0.0, a: 1.0 },
    loadOp: "clear",
    storeOp: "store"
  }]
});
renderPass.setPipeline(renderPipeline);
renderPass.draw(3, 1, 0, 0); // Draw a triangle
renderPass.end();

// Finish encoding and submit to GPU
const commandBuffer = commandEncoder.finish();
device.queue.submit([commandBuffer]);

value.docs:
The searchParams property of the URL interface provides a direct interface to query parameters through a URLSearchParams object.

This property offers a convenient way to:

  • Parse URL query parameters
  • Manipulate query strings
  • Add, modify, or delete URL parameters
  • Work with form data in a URL-encoded format
  • Handle query string encoding/decoding automatically

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Parse and access query parameters from a URL
const myURL = new URL('https://example.org/search?term=deno&page=2&sort=desc');
const params = myURL.searchParams;

console.log(params.get('term'));  // Logs "deno"
console.log(params.get('page'));  // Logs "2"

// Check if a parameter exists
console.log(params.has('sort'));  // Logs true

// Add or modify parameters (automatically updates the URL)
params.append('filter', 'recent');
params.set('page', '3');
console.log(myURL.href);  // URL is updated with new parameters

// Remove a parameter
params.delete('sort');

// Iterate over all parameters
for (const [key, value] of params) {
  console.log(`${key}: ${value}`);
}

content.name: invertSelf
content.js_doc:
The invertSelf() method of the DOMMatrix interface inverts the original matrix. If the matrix cannot be inverted, the new matrix's components are all set to NaN and its is2D property is set to false.

MDN Reference

content.name: multiplySelf
content.js_doc:
The multiplySelf() method of the DOMMatrix interface multiplies a matrix by the otherMatrix parameter, computing the dot product of the original matrix and the specified matrix: A⋅B. If no matrix is specified as the multiplier, the matrix is multiplied by a matrix in which every element is 0 except the bottom-right corner and the element immediately above and to its left: m33 and m34. These have the default value of 1.

MDN Reference

content.name: preMultiplySelf
content.js_doc:
The preMultiplySelf() method of the DOMMatrix interface modifies the matrix by pre-multiplying it with the specified DOMMatrix. This is equivalent to the dot product B⋅A, where matrix A is the source matrix and B is the matrix given as an input to the method. If no matrix is specified as the multiplier, the matrix is multiplied by a matrix in which every element is 0 except the bottom-right corner and the element immediately above and to its left: m33 and m34. These have the default value of 1.

MDN Reference

content.name: rotateAxisAngleSelf
content.js_doc:
The rotateAxisAngleSelf() method of the DOMMatrix interface is a transformation method that rotates the source matrix by the given vector and angle, returning the altered matrix.

MDN Reference

content.name: rotateFromVectorSelf
content.js_doc:
The rotateFromVectorSelf() method of the DOMMatrix interface is a mutable transformation method that modifies a matrix by rotating the matrix by the angle between the specified vector and (1, 0). The rotation angle is determined by the angle between the vector (1,0)T and (x,y)T in the clockwise direction, or (+/-)arctan(y/x). If x and y are both 0, the angle is specified as 0, and the matrix is not altered.

MDN Reference

content.name: rotateSelf
content.js_doc:
The rotateSelf() method of the DOMMatrix interface is a mutable transformation method that modifies a matrix. It rotates the source matrix around each of its axes by the specified number of degrees and returns the rotated matrix.

MDN Reference

content.name: scale3dSelf
content.js_doc:
The scale3dSelf() method of the DOMMatrix interface is a mutable transformation method that modifies a matrix by applying a specified scaling factor to all three axes, centered on the given origin, with a default origin of (0, 0, 0), returning the 3D-scaled matrix.

MDN Reference

content.name: scaleSelf
content.js_doc:
The scaleSelf() method of the DOMMatrix interface is a mutable transformation method that modifies a matrix by applying a specified scaling factor, centered on the given origin, with a default origin of (0, 0), returning the scaled matrix.

MDN Reference

content.name: setMatrixValue
content.js_doc:
The setMatrixValue() method of the DOMMatrix interface replaces the contents of the matrix with the matrix described by the specified transform or transforms, returning itself.

MDN Reference

content.name: skewXSelf
content.js_doc:
The skewXSelf() method of the DOMMatrix interface is a mutable transformation method that modifies a matrix. It skews the source matrix by applying the specified skew transformation along the X-axis and returns the skewed matrix.

MDN Reference

content.docs:
Creates a deep copy of a given value using the structured clone algorithm.

Unlike a shallow copy, a deep copy does not hold the same references as the source object, meaning its properties can be changed without affecting the source. For more details, see MDN.

Throws a DataCloneError if any part of the input value is not serializable.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
const object = { x: 0, y: 1 };

const deepCopy = structuredClone(object);
deepCopy.x = 1;
console.log(deepCopy.x, object.x); // 1 0

const shallowCopy = object;
shallowCopy.x = 1;
// shallowCopy.x is pointing to the same location in memory as object.x
console.log(shallowCopy.x, object.x); // 1 1

// Create a buffer that can be used as a vertex buffer and can be written to
const vertexBuffer = device.createBuffer({
  label: "Vertex Buffer",
  size: vertices.byteLength,
  usage: GPUBufferUsage.VERTEX | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST,
});

// Write data to the buffer
device.queue.writeBuffer(vertexBuffer, 0, vertices);

// Example of creating a mapped buffer for CPU access
const stagingBuffer = device.createBuffer({
  size: data.byteLength,
  usage: GPUBufferUsage.MAP_WRITE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_SRC,
  mappedAtCreation: true,
});

// Copy data to the mapped buffer
new Uint8Array(stagingBuffer.getMappedRange()).set(data);
stagingBuffer.unmap();

content.docs:
Creates a unique, temporary URL that represents a given Blob, File, or MediaSource object.

This method is particularly useful for:

  • Creating URLs for dynamically generated content
  • Working with blobs in a browser context
  • Creating workers from dynamically generated code
  • Setting up temporary URL references for file downloads

Note: Always call URL.revokeObjectURL() when you're done using the URL to prevent memory leaks.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Create a URL string for a Blob
const blob = new Blob(["Hello, world!"], { type: "text/plain" });
const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
console.log(url);  // Logs something like "blob:null/1234-5678-9101-1121"

// Dynamic web worker creation in Deno
const workerCode = `
  self.onmessage = (e) => {
    self.postMessage(e.data.toUpperCase());
  };
`;
const workerBlob = new Blob([workerCode], { type: "application/javascript" });
const workerUrl = URL.createObjectURL(workerBlob);
const worker = new Worker(workerUrl, { type: "module" });

worker.onmessage = (e) => console.log(e.data);
worker.postMessage("hello from deno");

// Always revoke when done to prevent memory leaks
URL.revokeObjectURL(workerUrl);

// Request an adapter with specific power preference
const adapter = await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter({
  powerPreference: "high-performance"

// Check adapter capabilities
if (adapter.features.has("shader-f16")) {
  console.log("Adapter supports 16-bit shader operations");

console.log(`GPU Device: ${adapter.info.device}`);

// Request a logical device with specific features and limits
const device = await adapter.requestDevice({
  requiredFeatures: ["shader-f16"],
  requiredLimits: {
    maxStorageBufferBindingSize: 128 * 1024 * 1024, // 128MB
  }
});

value.docs:
Deno's sessionStorage API operates similarly to the localStorage API, but it is intended for storing data temporarily for the duration of a session. Data stored in sessionStorage is cleared when the application session or process ends. This makes it suitable for temporary data that you do not need to persist across user sessions.

  • Key-Value Storage: Stores data as key-value pairs.
  • Session-Based: Data is only available for the duration of the page session.
  • Synchronous API: Operations are performed synchronously.

sessionStorage is similar to localStorage, and shares the same API methods, visible in the Storage type.

For more information, see the reference guide for Web Storage

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Set a value in sessionStorage
sessionStorage.setItem("key", "value");

// Get a value from sessionStorage
const value = sessionStorage.getItem("key");
console.log(value); // Output: "value"

// Remove a value from sessionStorage
sessionStorage.removeItem("key");

// Clear all the values from sessionStorage
sessionStorage.clear();

value.docs:
Provides the API for creating and managing a WebSocket connection to a server, as well as for sending and receiving data on the connection.

If you are looking to create a WebSocket server, please take a look at Deno.upgradeWebSocket().

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Creating a WebSocket connection
const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8080");

// Setting up event handlers
ws.onopen = (event) => {
  console.log("Connected to the server");
  ws.send("Hello Server!");
};

ws.onmessage = (event) => {
  console.log(`Received: ${event.data}`);
};

ws.onerror = (event) => {
  console.error("WebSocket error observed:", event);
};

ws.onclose = (event) => {
  console.log(`WebSocket closed: Code=${event.code}, Reason=${event.reason}`);
};

content.name: binaryType
content.js_doc:
Returns a string that indicates how binary data from the WebSocket object is exposed to scripts:

Can be set, to change how binary data is returned. The default is "blob".

const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8080");
ws.binaryType = "arraybuffer";

content.name: bufferedAmount
content.js_doc:
Returns the number of bytes of application data (UTF-8 text and binary data) that have been queued using send() but not yet been transmitted to the network.

If the WebSocket connection is closed, this attribute's value will only increase with each call to the send() method. (The number does not reset to zero once the connection closes.)

const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8080");
ws.send("Hello, world!");
console.log(ws.bufferedAmount); // 13

content.name: extensions
content.js_doc:
Returns the extensions selected by the server, if any.

WebSocket extensions add optional features negotiated during the handshake via the Sec-WebSocket-Extensions header.

At the time of writing, there are two registered extensions:

  • permessage-deflate: Enables per-message compression using DEFLATE.
  • bbf-usp-protocol: Used by the Broadband Forum's User Services Platform (USP).

See the full list at IANA WebSocket Extensions.

Example:

const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8080");
console.log(ws.extensions); // e.g., "permessage-deflate"

content.name: protocol
content.js_doc: Returns the subprotocol selected by the server, if any. It can be used in conjunction with the array form of the constructor's second argument to perform subprotocol negotiation.

content.name: readyState
content.js_doc: Returns the state of the WebSocket object's connection. It can have the values described below.

content.name: url
content.js_doc: Returns the URL that was used to establish the WebSocket connection.

content.name: close
content.js_doc: Closes the WebSocket connection, optionally using code as the WebSocket connection close code and reason as the WebSocket connection close reason.

content.name: send
content.js_doc: Transmits data using the WebSocket connection. data can be a string, a Blob, an ArrayBuffer, or an ArrayBufferView.

value.docs: The global CacheStorage instance, providing access to the named Cache objects used to store and retrieve Request/Response pairs.
Provides access to the Cache API. Returns a CacheStorage object, which enables storing, retrieving, and managing request/response pairs in a cache.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Open (or create) a cache
const cache = await caches.open('v1');

// Store a response
await cache.put('/api/data', new Response('Hello World'));

// Retrieve from cache with fallback
const response = await caches.match('/api/data') || await fetch('/api/data');

// Delete specific cache
await caches.delete('v1');

// List all cache names
const cacheNames = await caches.keys();

// Cache-first strategy
async function fetchWithCache(request) {
  const cached = await caches.match(request);
  if (cached) return cached;

  const response = await fetch(request);
  const cache = await caches.open('v1');
  await cache.put(request, response.clone());
  return response;
}

content.name: deno
content.js_doc:
Configure permissions options to change the level of access the worker will have. By default it will inherit permissions. Note that the permissions of a worker can't be extended beyond its parent's permissions reach.

  • "inherit" will use the default behavior and take the permissions of the thread the worker is created in
  • "none" will have no permissions
  • A list of routes can be provided that are relative to the file the worker is created in to limit the access of the worker (read/write permissions only)

Example:

// mod.ts
const worker = new Worker(
  new URL("deno_worker.ts", import.meta.url).href, {
    type: "module",
    deno: {
      permissions: {
        read: true,
      },
    },
  }
);

The CloseEvent interface represents an event that occurs when a WebSocket connection is closed.

This event is sent to the client when the connection is closed, providing information about why the connection was closed through the code, reason, and wasClean properties.

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Handling a close event
ws.addEventListener("close", (event: CloseEvent) => {
  console.log(`Connection closed with code ${event.code}`);
  console.log(`Reason: ${event.reason}`);
  console.log(`Clean close: ${event.wasClean}`);

  if (event.code === 1006) {
    console.log("Connection closed abnormally");
  }
});

content.name: code
content.js_doc: Returns the WebSocket connection close code provided by the server.

content.name: reason
content.js_doc: Returns the WebSocket connection close reason provided by the server.

content.name: wasClean
content.js_doc: Returns true if the connection closed cleanly; false otherwise.

  wasClean: true,
});

The WebAssembly JavaScript object acts as the namespace for all WebAssembly-related functionality. Unlike most global objects, it is not a constructor; it groups the functions used to compile and instantiate WebAssembly modules together with the classes (Module, Instance, Memory, Table, Global) and error types used to work with them.

EventTarget is a DOM interface implemented by objects that can receive events and may have listeners for them.

content.name: addEventListener
content.js_doc:
Appends an event listener for events whose type attribute value is type. The callback argument sets the callback that will be invoked when the event is dispatched.

The options argument sets listener-specific options. For compatibility this can be a boolean, in which case the method behaves exactly as if the value was specified as options's capture.

When set to true, options's capture prevents callback from being invoked when the event's eventPhase attribute value is BUBBLING_PHASE. When false (or not present), callback will not be invoked when event's eventPhase attribute value is CAPTURING_PHASE. Either way, callback will be invoked if event's eventPhase attribute value is AT_TARGET.

When set to true, options's passive indicates that the callback will not cancel the event by invoking preventDefault(). This is used to enable performance optimizations described in § 2.8 Observing event listeners.

When set to true, options's once indicates that the callback will only be invoked once after which the event listener will be removed.

The event listener is appended to target's event listener list and is not appended if it has the same type, callback, and capture.

content.name: dispatchEvent
content.js_doc: Dispatches a synthetic event to event target and returns true if either event's cancelable attribute value is false or its preventDefault() method was not invoked, and false otherwise.

content.name: removeEventListener
content.js_doc: Removes the event listener in target's event listener list with the same type, callback, and options.

const pattern = new URLPattern("https://example.com/books/:id");

content.docs:
Match the given input against the stored pattern.

The input can either be provided as an absolute URL string with an optional base, relative URL string with a required base, or as individual components in the form of an URLPatternInit object.

const pattern = new URLPattern("https://example.com/books/:id");

// Match an absolute url string.
let match = pattern.exec("https://example.com/books/123");
console.log(match.pathname.groups.id); // 123

// Match a relative url with a base.
match = pattern.exec("/books/123", "https://example.com");
console.log(match.pathname.groups.id); // 123

// Match an object of url components.
match = pattern.exec({ pathname: "/books/123" });
console.log(match.pathname.groups.id); // 123
