content.name: Console
content.docs: The Console interface provides methods for logging information to the console, as well as other utility methods for debugging and inspecting code. Methods include logging, debugging, and timing functionality.

content.name: console
content.docs: A global console object that provides methods for logging, debugging, and error reporting. The console object provides access to the browser's or runtime's debugging console functionality. It allows developers to output text and data for debugging purposes.

content.name: CountQueuingStrategy
content.docs: This Streams API interface provides a built-in byte length queuing strategy that can be used when constructing streams.

content.name: createImageBitmap
content.docs: Create a new ImageBitmap object from a given source.

content.name: Crypto
content.docs: This Web Crypto API interface provides basic cryptographic functionality. It is accessed via the global crypto property, which gives access to cryptographically strong random number generation and to the low-level primitives exposed by SubtleCrypto through Crypto.subtle.

content.name: crypto
content.docs: The global instance of Crypto that provides access to the Web Crypto API, including cryptographically secure random number generation via Crypto.getRandomValues, random UUID generation via Crypto.randomUUID, and the low-level primitives exposed by SubtleCrypto through Crypto.subtle.

content.name: CryptoKey
content.docs: The CryptoKey dictionary of the Web Crypto API represents a cryptographic key.

content.name: CryptoKeyPair
content.docs: The CryptoKeyPair dictionary of the Web Crypto API represents a key pair for an asymmetric cryptography algorithm, also known as a public-key algorithm.

content.name: CSSRule
content.docs: A single CSS rule of a CSSStyleSheet, as returned from its cssRules property. Available only when the --unstable-raw-imports flag is enabled.

content.name: CSSStyleSheet
content.docs: A style sheet backing a CSS module script. This is what a import sheet from "./styles.css" with { type: "css" } import evaluates to. Available only when the --unstable-raw-imports flag is enabled.

content.name: DecompressionStream
content.docs: An API for decompressing a stream of data.

content.name: dispatchEvent
content.docs: Dispatches an event in the global scope, synchronously invoking any registered event listeners for this event in the appropriate order. Returns false if event is cancelable and at least one of the event handlers which handled this event called Event.preventDefault(). Otherwise it returns true.

content.name: DOMMatrix
content.docs: The DOMMatrix interface represents 4×4 matrices, suitable for 2D and 3D operations including rotation and translation. It is a mutable version of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface. The interface is available inside web workers.

content.name: DOMMatrixReadOnly
content.docs: The DOMMatrixReadOnly interface represents a read-only 4×4 matrix, suitable for 2D and 3D operations. The DOMMatrix interface — which is based upon DOMMatrixReadOnly—adds mutability, allowing you to alter the matrix after creating it.

content.name: DOMPoint
content.docs: A DOMPoint object represents a 2D or 3D point in a coordinate system; it includes values for the coordinates in up to three dimensions, as well as an optional perspective value. DOMPoint is based on DOMPointReadOnly but allows its properties' values to be changed.

content.name: DOMPointReadOnly
content.docs: The DOMPointReadOnly interface specifies the coordinate and perspective fields used by DOMPoint to define a 2D or 3D point in a coordinate system.

content.name: DOMQuad
content.docs: A DOMQuad is a collection of four DOMPoints defining the corners of an arbitrary quadrilateral. Returning DOMQuads lets getBoxQuads() return accurate information even when arbitrary 2D or 3D transforms are present. It has a handy bounds attribute returning a DOMRectReadOnly for those cases where you just want an axis-aligned bounding rectangle.

content.name: DOMRect
content.docs: A DOMRect describes the size and position of a rectangle.

content.name: DOMRectReadOnly
content.docs: The DOMRectReadOnly interface specifies the standard properties (also used by DOMRect) to define a rectangle whose properties are immutable.

content.name: Event
content.docs: An event which takes place in the DOM.

content.name: EventListenerObject
content.docs: The EventListenerObject interface represents an object that can handle events dispatched by an EventTarget object.

content.name: EventSource
content.docs: Represents a connection to a server that sends server-sent events, receiving updates pushed by the server as a stream of message events over a persistent HTTP connection that automatically reconnects when interrupted.

content.name: EventTarget
content.docs: EventTarget is a DOM interface implemented by objects that can receive events and may have listeners for them.

content.name: fetch
content.docs: Fetch a resource from the network. It returns a Promise that resolves to the Response to that Request, whether it is successful or not.

content.name: File
content.docs: Provides information about files and allows JavaScript in a web page to access their content.

content.name: FileReader
content.docs: Lets web applications asynchronously read the contents of files (or raw data buffers) stored on the user's computer, using File or Blob objects to specify the file or data to read.

content.name: FormData
content.docs: Provides a way to easily construct a set of key/value pairs representing form fields and their values, which can then be easily sent using the XMLHttpRequest.send() method. It uses the same format a form would use if the encoding type were set to "multipart/form-data".

content.name: GPU
content.docs: The entry point to WebGPU in Deno, accessed via the global navigator.gpu property.

content.name: GPUAdapter
content.docs: Represents a physical GPU device that can be used to create a logical GPU device.

content.name: GPUBuffer
content.docs: Represents a block of memory allocated on the GPU.

content.name: GPUCanvasContext
content.docs: The rendering context that presents WebGPU-rendered images on an OffscreenCanvas. Obtained from OffscreenCanvas.getContext with the "webgpu" context id.

content.name: GPUCommandEncoder
content.docs: Used to record GPU commands for later execution by the GPU.

content.name: GPUDevice
content.docs: The primary interface for interacting with a WebGPU device.

content.name: GPUError
content.docs: The GPUError interface of the WebGPU API is the base interface for errors surfaced by GPUDevice.popErrorScope and the GPUDevice.uncapturederror_event event. Available only in secure contexts.

content.name: GPUPipelineError
content.docs: The GPUPipelineError interface of the WebGPU API describes a pipeline failure. Available only in secure contexts.

content.name: GPUQueue
content.docs: Represents a queue to submit commands to the GPU.

content.name: GPUShaderModule
content.docs: Represents a compiled shader module that can be used to create graphics or compute pipelines.

content.name: GPUTexture
content.docs: Represents a texture (image) in GPU memory.

content.name: Headers
content.docs: This Fetch API interface allows you to perform various actions on HTTP request and response headers. These actions include retrieving, setting, adding to, and removing. A Headers object has an associated header list, which is initially empty and consists of zero or more name and value pairs. You can add to this using methods like append() (see Examples). In all methods of this interface, header names are matched by case-insensitive byte sequence.

content.name: ImageBitmap
content.docs: ImageBitmap interface represents a bitmap image which can be drawn to a canvas.

content.name: ImageBitmapOptions
content.docs: The options of createImageBitmap.

content.name: ImageBitmapRenderingContext
content.docs: A rendering context that displays the contents of an ImageBitmap on an OffscreenCanvas. Obtained from OffscreenCanvas.getContext with the "bitmaprenderer" context id.

content.name: ImageBitmapSource
content.docs: The ImageBitmapSource type represents an image data source that can be used to create an ImageBitmap.

content.name: ImageOrientation
content.docs: Specifies how the bitmap image should be oriented.

content.name: ImportMeta
content.docs: Deno provides extra properties on import.meta. These are included here to ensure that these are still available when using the Deno namespace in conjunction with other type libs, like dom.

content.name: Intl
content.docs: The Intl namespace groups the ECMAScript Internationalization API constructors and functions.

content.name: Intl.DateTimeFormatRangePart
content.docs: Represents a part of a formatted date range produced by Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatRange().

content.name: Intl.Formattable
content.docs: Types that can be formatted using Intl.DateTimeFormat methods.

content.name: Intl.Locale
content.docs: Augments the standard Intl.Locale interface with members not yet present in the bundled TypeScript library definitions.

content.name: localStorage
content.docs: Deno's localStorage API provides a way to store key-value pairs in a web-like environment, similar to the Web Storage API found in browsers. It allows developers to persist data across sessions in a Deno application. This API is particularly useful for applications that require a simple and effective way to store data locally.

content.name: Location
content.docs: The location (URL) of the object it is linked to. Changes done on it are reflected on the object it relates to. Accessible via globalThis.location.

content.name: location
content.docs: The Location object describing the absolute URL of the main module, available when the program is started with the --location flag. Accessing it without --location throws.

content.name: MessageChannel
content.docs: The MessageChannel interface of the Channel Messaging API allows us to create a new message channel and send data through it via its two MessagePort properties.

content.name: MessagePort
content.docs: The MessagePort interface of the Channel Messaging API represents one of the two ports of a MessageChannel, allowing messages to be sent from one port and listening out for them arriving at the other.

content.name: name
content.docs: Gets or sets the name of the global scope's browsing context.

content.name: Navigator
content.docs: Provides information about the Deno runtime environment and the system on which it's running. Similar to the browser Navigator object but adapted for the Deno context.

content.name: navigator
content.docs: Provides access to the Deno runtime's Navigator interface, which contains information about the environment in which the script is running.

content.name: NavigatorUABrandVersion
content.docs: A brand and version pair describing a user agent, as returned by NavigatorUAData.

content.name: NavigatorUAData
content.docs: Gives access to information about the runtime's user agent, exposed via Navigator.userAgentData. This is the User-Agent Client Hints API.

content.name: OffscreenCanvas
content.docs: A canvas that can be rendered to off the main thread and without being attached to the DOM. It exposes drawing contexts via OffscreenCanvas.getContext and can produce a Blob or ImageBitmap from its contents.

content.name: onbeforeunload
content.docs: Before unload event handler for the window. In Deno, this is primarily for API compatibility with browsers.

content.name: onerror
content.docs: Error event handler for the window. Triggered when an uncaught error occurs in the global scope.

content.name: onload
content.docs: Load event handler for the window. In Deno, this is primarily for API compatibility with browsers.

content.name: onunhandledrejection
content.docs: Event handler for unhandled promise rejections. Triggered when a Promise is rejected and no rejection handler is attached to it.

content.name: onunload
content.docs: Unload event handler for the window. In Deno, this is primarily for API compatibility with browsers.

content.name: Performance
content.docs: Deno supports User Timing Level 3 which is not widely supported yet in other runtimes.

content.name: performance
content.docs: The global Performance instance, providing access to high-resolution timing via performance.now() and the user-timing marks and measures APIs.

content.name: PerformanceEntry
content.docs: Encapsulates a single performance metric that is part of the performance timeline. A performance entry can be directly created by making a performance mark or measure (for example by calling the .mark() method) at an explicit point in an application.

content.name: PerformanceMark
content.docs: PerformanceMark is an abstract interface for PerformanceEntry objects with an entryType of "mark". Entries of this type are created by calling performance.mark() to add a named DOMHighResTimeStamp (the mark) to the performance timeline.

content.name: PerformanceMarkOptions
content.docs: Options which are used in conjunction with performance.mark. Check out the MDN performance.mark() documentation for more details.

content.name: PerformanceMeasure
content.docs: PerformanceMeasure is an abstract interface for PerformanceEntry objects with an entryType of "measure". Entries of this type are created by calling performance.measure() to add a named DOMHighResTimeStamp (the measure) between two marks to the performance timeline.

content.name: PerformanceMeasureOptions
content.docs: Options which are used in conjunction with performance.measure. Check out the MDN performance.mark() documentation for more details.

content.name: PerformanceObserver
content.docs: Observes performance measurement events and is notified of new PerformanceEntry objects as they are recorded in the performance timeline.

content.name: PerformanceObserverCallback
content.docs: The callback invoked when the observed set of performance entries grows.

content.name: PerformanceObserverEntryList
content.docs: A list of PerformanceEntry objects passed to a PerformanceObserver callback via its observe() method.

content.name: PremultiplyAlpha
content.docs: Specifies whether the bitmap's color channels should be premultiplied by the alpha channel.

content.name: ProgressEvent
content.docs: Events measuring progress of an underlying process, like an HTTP request (for an XMLHttpRequest, or the loading of the underlying resource of an ,

content.name: prompt
content.docs: Shows the given message and waits for the user's input. Returns the user's input as string.

content.name: queueMicrotask
content.docs: A microtask is a short function which is executed after the function or module which created it exits and only if the JavaScript execution stack is empty, but before returning control to the event loop being used to drive the script's execution environment. This event loop may be either the main event loop or the event loop driving a web worker.

content.name: QuotaExceededError
content.docs: Represents an error when a quota has been exceeded.

content.name: ReadableStream
content.docs: This Streams API interface represents a readable stream of byte data. The Fetch API offers a concrete instance of a ReadableStream through the body property of a Response object.

content.name: removeEventListener
content.docs: Remove a previously registered event listener from the global scope

content.name: reportError
content.docs: Dispatch an uncaught exception. Similar to a synchronous version of:

content.name: Request
content.docs: This Fetch API interface represents a resource request.

content.name: ResizeQuality
content.docs: Specifies the algorithm to be used for resizing the input to match the output dimensions. One of pixelated, low (default), medium, or high.

content.name: Response
content.docs: This Fetch API interface represents the response to a request.

content.name: self
content.docs: Reference to the global object itself. Equivalent to the global window object in browser environments.

content.name: sessionStorage
content.docs: Deno's sessionStorage API operates similarly to the localStorage API, but it is intended for storing data temporarily for the duration of a session. Data stored in sessionStorage is cleared when the application session or process ends. This makes it suitable for temporary data that you do not need to persist across user sessions.

content.name: Storage
content.docs: This Web Storage API interface provides access to a particular domain's session or local storage. It allows, for example, the addition, modification, or deletion of stored data items.

content.name: structuredClone
content.docs: Creates a deep copy of a given value using the structured clone algorithm.

content.name: StructuredSerializeOptions
content.docs: Options that control structured serialization operations such as structuredClone(value, options) and MessagePort.postMessage(message, options).

content.name: SubtleCrypto
content.docs: This Web Crypto API interface provides a number of low-level cryptographic functions. It is accessed via the Crypto.subtle properties available in a window context (via globalThis.crypto).

content.name: TextDecoder
content.docs: Represents a decoder for a specific text encoding, allowing you to convert binary data into a string given the encoding.

content.name: TextEncoder
content.docs: Allows you to convert a string into binary data (in the form of a Uint8Array) given the encoding.

content.name: UADataValues
content.docs: The values returned by NavigatorUAData.getHighEntropyValues.

content.name: UALowEntropyJSON
content.docs: The low-entropy values returned by NavigatorUAData.toJSON.

content.name: URL
content.docs: The URL interface represents an object providing static methods used for creating, parsing, and manipulating URLs in Deno.

content.name: URLPattern
content.docs: The URLPattern API provides a web platform primitive for matching URLs based on a convenient pattern syntax.

content.name: URLPatternOptions
content.docs: Options for the URLPattern constructor.

content.name: URLPatternResult
content.docs: URLPatternResult is the object returned from URLPattern.exec.

content.name: URLSearchParams
content.docs: URLSearchParams provides methods for working with the query string of a URL.

content.name: URLSearchParamsIterator
content.docs: Iterator for the URLSearchParams class, used to iterate over key-value pairs in search parameters.

content.name: WebAssembly
content.docs: The WebAssembly JavaScript object acts as the namespace for all WebAssembly-related functionality. Unlike most global objects, it is not a constructor; it groups the functions used to compile and instantiate WebAssembly modules together with the classes (Module, Instance, Memory, Table, Global) and error types used to work with them.

content.name: WebAssembly.compile
content.docs: The WebAssembly.compile() function compiles WebAssembly binary code into a WebAssembly.Module object. This function is useful if it is necessary to compile a module before it can be instantiated (otherwise, the WebAssembly.instantiate() function should be used).

content.name: WebAssembly.CompileError
content.docs: The WebAssembly.CompileError object indicates an error during WebAssembly decoding or validation.

content.name: WebAssembly.compileStreaming
content.docs: The WebAssembly.compileStreaming() function compiles a WebAssembly.Module directly from a streamed underlying source. This function is useful if it is necessary to a compile a module before it can be instantiated (otherwise, the WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming() function should be used).

content.name: WebAssembly.Exports
content.docs: The set of values exported by a WebAssembly module instance, keyed by export name.

content.name: WebAssembly.ExportValue
content.docs: A value that can be exported from a WebAssembly module instance.

content.name: WebAssembly.Global
content.docs: A WebAssembly.Global object represents a global variable instance, accessible from both JavaScript and importable/exportable across one or more WebAssembly.Module instances. This allows dynamic linking of multiple modules.

content.name: WebAssembly.GlobalDescriptor
content.docs: The GlobalDescriptor describes the options you can pass to new WebAssembly.Global().

content.name: WebAssembly.ImportExportKind
content.docs: The kind of entity referenced by a module import or export descriptor.

content.name: WebAssembly.Imports
content.docs: The import object supplied when instantiating a WebAssembly module, grouping imported values by module name.

content.name: WebAssembly.ImportValue
content.docs: A value that can be supplied to a WebAssembly module as an import.

content.name: WebAssembly.Instance
content.docs: A WebAssembly.Instance object is a stateful, executable instance of a WebAssembly.Module. Instance objects contain all the Exported WebAssembly functions that allow calling into WebAssembly code from JavaScript.

content.name: WebAssembly.instantiate
content.docs: The WebAssembly.instantiate() function allows you to compile and instantiate WebAssembly code.

content.name: WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming
content.docs: The WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming() function compiles and instantiates a WebAssembly module directly from a streamed underlying source. This is the most efficient, optimized way to load wasm code.

content.name: WebAssembly.LinkError
content.docs: The WebAssembly.LinkError object indicates an error during module instantiation (besides traps from the start function).

content.name: WebAssembly.Memory
content.docs: The WebAssembly.Memory object is a resizable ArrayBuffer or SharedArrayBuffer that holds the raw bytes of memory accessed by a WebAssembly Instance.

content.name: WebAssembly.MemoryDescriptor
content.docs: The MemoryDescriptor describes the options you can pass to new WebAssembly.Memory().

content.name: WebAssembly.Module
content.docs: A WebAssembly.Module object contains stateless WebAssembly code that has already been compiled by the browser — this can be efficiently shared with Workers, and instantiated multiple times.

content.name: WebAssembly.ModuleExportDescriptor
content.docs: A ModuleExportDescriptor is the description of a declared export in a WebAssembly.Module.

content.name: WebAssembly.ModuleImportDescriptor
content.docs: A ModuleImportDescriptor is the description of a declared import in a WebAssembly.Module.

content.name: WebAssembly.ModuleImports
content.docs: The set of values imported from a single module, keyed by import name.

content.name: WebAssembly.RuntimeError
content.docs: The WebAssembly.RuntimeError object is the error type that is thrown whenever WebAssembly specifies a trap.

content.name: WebAssembly.Table
content.docs: The WebAssembly.Table() object is a JavaScript wrapper object — an array-like structure representing a WebAssembly Table, which stores function references. A table created by JavaScript or in WebAssembly code will be accessible and mutable from both JavaScript and WebAssembly.

content.name: WebAssembly.TableDescriptor
content.docs: The TableDescriptor describes the options you can pass to new WebAssembly.Table().

content.name: WebAssembly.TableKind
content.docs: The type of value stored in a WebAssembly.Table.

content.name: WebAssembly.validate
content.docs: The WebAssembly.validate() function validates a given typed array of WebAssembly binary code, returning whether the bytes form a valid wasm module (true) or not (false).

content.name: WebAssembly.ValueType
content.docs: The data type of a WebAssembly value, used to describe globals.

content.name: WebAssembly.WebAssemblyInstantiatedSource
content.docs: The value returned from WebAssembly.instantiate.

content.name: WebSocket
content.docs: Provides the API for creating and managing a WebSocket connection to a server, as well as for sending and receiving data on the connection.

content.name: WebSocketEventMap
content.docs: Interface mapping WebSocket event names to their corresponding event types. Used for strongly typed event handling with addEventListener and removeEventListener.

content.name: WebSocketOptions
content.docs: Options for a WebSocket instance. This feature is non-standard.

content.name: WebTransport
content.docs: MDN Reference

content.name: WebTransportBidirectionalStream
content.docs: MDN Reference

content.name: WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream
content.docs: MDN Reference

content.name: WebTransportError
content.docs: MDN Reference

content.name: WebTransportReceiveStream
content.docs: MDN Reference

content.name: WebTransportSendGroup
content.docs: MDN Reference

content.name: WebTransportSendStream
content.docs: MDN Reference

content.name: WebTransportWriter
content.docs: MDN Reference

content.name: Window
content.docs: Represents the global window object in the Deno runtime environment.

content.name: WindowEventMap
content.docs: Defines the mapping between event names and their corresponding event types for the Window interface in Deno.

content.name: Worker
content.docs: The Worker interface represents a background task that can be created via the new Worker() constructor. Workers run in a separate thread, allowing for parallel execution without blocking the main thread.

content.name: WritableStream
content.docs: This Streams API interface provides a standard abstraction for writing streaming data to a destination, known as a sink. This object comes with built-in backpressure and queuing.

content.name: WritableStreamDefaultController
content.docs: This Streams API interface represents a controller allowing control of a WritableStream's state. When constructing a WritableStream, the underlying sink is given a corresponding WritableStreamDefaultController instance to manipulate.

content.name: WritableStreamDefaultWriter
content.docs: This Streams API interface is the object returned by WritableStream.getWriter() and once created locks the < writer to the WritableStream ensuring that no other streams can write to the underlying sink.

How is the API different from browsers?

  2. You cannot pass options like ignoreVary, ignoreMethod, ignoreSearch.

Delete cache object matching the provided request.

How is the API different from browsers?

  2. You cannot pass options like ignoreVary, ignoreMethod, ignoreSearch.

value.docs:
The Worker interface represents a background task that can be created via the new Worker() constructor. Workers run in a separate thread, allowing for parallel execution without blocking the main thread.

Workers can be used to:

  • Perform CPU-intensive calculations
  • Process large datasets
  • Handle tasks in parallel with the main execution thread
  • Run code in isolation with its own event loop

content.title: Example 1
content.markdown_body:
// Creating a basic worker (main.ts)
const worker = new Worker(new URL("./worker.ts", import.meta.url).href, {
  type: "module"
});

// Send data to the worker
worker.postMessage({ command: "start", data: [1, 2, 3, 4] });

// Receive messages from the worker
worker.onmessage = (e) => {
  console.log("Result from worker:", e.data);
  worker.terminate(); // Stop the worker when done
};

// Handle worker errors
worker.onerror = (e) => {
  console.error("Worker error:", e.message);
};

content.title: Example 2
content.markdown_body:
// Worker file (worker.ts)
// Worker context: self refers to the worker's global scope
self.onmessage = (e) => {
  if (e.data.command === "start") {
    // Perform calculation with the data
    const result = e.data.data.reduce((sum, num) => sum + num, 0);
    // Send result back to main thread
    self.postMessage(result);
  }
};

Revokes a previously created object URL, freeing the memory associated with it.

Important for memory management in applications that create dynamic URLs. Once an object URL is revoked:

  • It can no longer be used to fetch the content it referenced
  • The browser/runtime is allowed to release the memory or resources associated with it
  • Workers created via the URL will continue to run, but the URL becomes invalid for new creations

For security and performance in Deno applications, always revoke object URLs as soon as they're no longer needed, especially when processing large files or generating many URLs.

content.name: flipX
content.js_doc:
The flipX() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface creates a new matrix being the result of the original matrix flipped about the x-axis. This is equivalent to multiplying the matrix by DOMMatrix(-1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0). The original matrix is not modified.

MDN Reference

content.name: flipY
content.js_doc:
The flipY() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface creates a new matrix being the result of the original matrix flipped about the y-axis. This is equivalent to multiplying the matrix by DOMMatrix(1, 0, 0, -1, 0, 0). The original matrix is not modified.

MDN Reference

content.name: inverse
content.js_doc:
The inverse() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface creates a new matrix which is the inverse of the original matrix. If the matrix cannot be inverted, the new matrix's components are all set to NaN and its is2D property is set to false. The original matrix is not changed.

MDN Reference

content.name: multiply
content.js_doc:
The multiply() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface creates and returns a new matrix which is the dot product of the matrix and the otherMatrix parameter. If otherMatrix is omitted, the matrix is multiplied by a matrix in which every element is 0 except the bottom-right corner and the element immediately above and to its left: m33 and m34. These have the default value of 1. The original matrix is not modified.

MDN Reference

content.name: rotate
content.js_doc:
The rotate() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface returns a new DOMMatrix created by rotating the source matrix around each of its axes by the specified number of degrees. The original matrix is not altered.

MDN Reference

content.name: rotateAxisAngle
content.js_doc:
The rotateAxisAngle() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface returns a new DOMMatrix created by rotating the source matrix by the given vector and angle. The original matrix is not altered.

MDN Reference

content.name: rotateFromVector
content.js_doc:
The rotateFromVector() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface is returns a new DOMMatrix created by rotating the source matrix by the angle between the specified vector and (1, 0). The rotation angle is determined by the angle between the vector (1,0)T and (x,y)T in the clockwise direction, or (+/-)arctan(y/x). If x and y are both 0, the angle is specified as 0. The original matrix is not altered.

MDN Reference

content.name: scale
content.js_doc:
The scale() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface creates a new matrix being the result of the original matrix with a scale transform applied.

MDN Reference

content.name: scale3d
content.js_doc:
The scale3d() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface creates a new matrix which is the result of a 3D scale transform being applied to the matrix. It returns a new DOMMatrix created by scaling the source 3d matrix by the given scale factor centered on the origin point specified by the origin parameters, with a default origin of (0, 0, 0). The original matrix is not modified.

MDN Reference

content.name: skewX
content.js_doc:
The skewX() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface returns a new DOMMatrix created by applying the specified skew transformation to the source matrix along its x-axis. The original matrix is not modified.

MDN Reference

content.name: skewY
content.js_doc:
The skewY() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface returns a new DOMMatrix created by applying the specified skew transformation to the source matrix along its y-axis. The original matrix is not modified.

MDN Reference

content.name: toFloat32Array
content.js_doc:
The toFloat32Array() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface returns a new Float32Array containing all 16 elements (m11, m12, m13, m14, m21, m22, m23, m24, m31, m32, m33, m34, m41, m42, m43, m44) which comprise the matrix. The elements are stored into the array as single-precision floating-point numbers in column-major (colexographical access, or "colex") order. (In other words, down the first column from top to bottom, then the second column, and so forth.)

MDN Reference

content.name: toFloat64Array
content.js_doc:
The toFloat64Array() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface returns a new Float64Array containing all 16 elements (m11, m12, m13, m14, m21, m22, m23, m24, m31, m32, m33, m34, m41, m42, m43, m44) which comprise the matrix. The elements are stored into the array as double-precision floating-point numbers in column-major (colexographical access, or "colex") order. (In other words, down the first column from top to bottom, then the second column, and so forth.)

content.name: toJSON
content.js_doc:
The toJSON() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface creates and returns a JSON object. The JSON object includes the 2D matrix elements a through f, the 16 elements of the 4X4 3D matrix, m[1-4][1-4], the boolean is2D property, and the boolean isIdentity property.

content.name: transformPoint
content.js_doc:
The transformPoint method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface creates a new DOMPoint object, transforming a specified point by the matrix. Neither the matrix nor the original point are altered.

content.name: translate

The translate() method of the DOMMatrixReadOnly interface creates a new matrix being the result of the original matrix with a translation applied.

value.docs:
The URL interface represents an object providing static methods used for creating, parsing, and manipulating URLs in Deno.

Use the URL API for safely parsing, constructing, normalizing, and encoding URLs. This is the preferred way to work with URLs in Deno rather than manual string manipulation which can lead to errors and security issues.

content.name: hash
content.js_doc: The hash property of the URL interface is a string that starts with a # and is followed by the fragment identifier of the URL. It returns an empty string if the URL does not contain a fragment identifier.

content.name: host
content.js_doc: The host property of the URL interface is a string that includes the URL.hostname and the URL.port if one is specified in the URL includes by including a : followed by the port number.

content.name: hostname
content.js_doc: The hostname property of the URL interface is a string that represents the fully qualified domain name of the URL.

content.name: href
content.js_doc: The href property of the URL interface is a string that represents the complete URL.

content.name: origin
content.js_doc: The origin property of the URL interface is a string that represents the origin of the URL, that is the URL.protocol, URL.host, and URL.port.

content.name: password
content.js_doc: The password property of the URL interface is a string that represents the password specified in the URL.

content.name: pathname
content.js_doc: The pathname property of the URL interface is a string that represents the path of the URL.

content.name: port
content.js_doc: The port property of the URL interface is a string that represents the port of the URL if an explicit port has been specified in the URL.

content.name: protocol
content.js_doc: The protocol property of the URL interface is a string that represents the protocol scheme of the URL and includes a trailing :.

content.name: search
content.js_doc: The search property of the URL interface is a string that represents the search string, or the query string, of the URL. This includes the ? character and the but excludes identifiers within the represented resource such as the URL.hash. More granular control can be found using URL.searchParams property.

content.name: searchParams
content.js_doc:
The searchParams property of the URL interface provides a direct interface to query parameters through a URLSearchParams object.

This property offers a convenient way to:

  • Parse URL query parameters
  • Manipulate query strings
  • Add, modify, or delete URL parameters
  • Work with form data in a URL-encoded format
  • Handle query string encoding/decoding automatically

content.name: username
content.js_doc: The username property of the URL interface is a string that represents the username of the URL.

content.name: toString
content.js_doc: The toString() method of the URL interface returns a string containing the complete URL.

content.name: toJSON
content.js_doc: The toJSON() method of the URL interface returns a JSON representation of the URL.

value.docs: The URL interface represents an object providing static methods used for creating, parsing, and manipulating URLs.

content.name: parse

content.name: canParse
content.js_doc: Returns a boolean value indicating if a URL string is valid and can be parsed.

content.name: createObjectURL
content.js_doc:
Creates a unique, temporary URL that represents a given Blob, File, or MediaSource object.

This method is particularly useful for:

  • Creating URLs for dynamically generated content
  • Working with blobs in a browser context
  • Creating workers from dynamically generated code
  • Setting up temporary URL references for file downloads

Note: Always call URL.revokeObjectURL() when you're done using the URL to prevent memory leaks.

content.name: revokeObjectURL
content.js_doc:
Revokes a previously created object URL, freeing the memory associated with it.

Important for memory management in applications that create dynamic URLs. Once an object URL is revoked:

  • It can no longer be used to fetch the content it referenced
  • The browser/runtime is allowed to release the memory or resources associated with it
  • Workers created via the URL will continue to run, but the URL becomes invalid for new creations

For security and performance in Deno applications, always revoke object URLs as soon as they're no longer needed, especially when processing large files or generating many URLs.
